input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: §2.1 is a multi-year take-or-pay commitment (USD 2,000,000 per year for three years) expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — squarely in walk-away territory and failing every fallback element: it is not limited to the current 12-month term, offers no 30-day reduction right, and provides no true-up in place of the shortfall penalty. It also contradicts §12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment, and sits uneasily with §7.1's bar on minimum-use charges. Because the commitment can be excised without collateral rewrites (no other provision cross-refers to it), we take the preferred position: no minimum purchase or volume commitment, with payment only for Services used or ordered. The exit/termination argument is left to T4C and is not duplicated here.

mappings.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.

proposal.summary: Replace the three-year take-or-pay commitment in §2.1 with a no-minimum-commitment, pay-for-use provision.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the USD 2,000,000 per year three-year take-or-pay commitment: our position is no minimum purchase or volume commitment, with fees payable only for Services used or ordered, which also aligns §2.1 with §12.3. If a commitment is essential, we could accept one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
